subject: FinTechX POC - Observability plan & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechx.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: FinTechX POC - Observability plan & success criteria

Hi Alex —

Great speaking with you this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned heading into the POC: 

Call recap (high level)
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood Inference for latency-sensitive customer-facing workflows and embedding search in FinTechX’s payments product.
- Success signals discussed: 1) 99th percentile generation latency target, 2) embedding recall/precision on sample dataset, 3) predictable cost per 1k tokens.

Proposed POC timeline (draft)
- Week 0: Access + baseline run (sample traffic)
- Week 1-2: Integration + observability dashboards live
- Week 3: Evaluation against success criteria, Final readout

Observability focus (what we’ll instrument during the POC)
- Dashboards: per-route latency (p50/p95/p99), token throughput, request rate, error rates, cost breakdown per route.
- Tracing: end-to-end traces from request -> model -> response, span breakdown for token generation, cache hit/miss tagging.
- Logs: structured request/response logs (with PII/redaction guidance), export hooks to your logging stack (S3/Datadog).
- Metrics to monitor: 99th percentile latency, median latency, errors per million requests, cache hit ratio, tokens generated per second, embedding similarity AUC for eval set.

Can you confirm:
1) the internal stakeholders who will own evaluation (you mentioned Priya and a platform engineer)
2) any constraints on log export or retention we should account for?

Next steps
- I’ll put together a detailed observability checklist and POC plan and share for review (includes dashboards, sample queries, and ownership).
- If that looks good, propose kickoff next week.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@fintechx.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 12:18:22 -0700
Subject: Re: FinTechX POC - Observability plan & success criteria

Thanks Marissa — good recap. A few clarifications / confirmation items from our side:

Success criteria (we’d like these measured during the POC)
- Latency: p99 generation latency < 300ms for 1k token responses on our test dataset.
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% under our baseline load.
- Cost: target < $X per 1k tokens (we’ll share a target number internally before kickoff).
- Quality: embedding-based retrieval improvement of >= 10% on our labeled eval set (we can provide the eval set).

Observability items
- Dashboards and traces look good — please include sample span names so our platform team can map them to our tracing UI.
- For logs: we need exports to our S3 bucket and optional forwarding to Datadog. Retention policy: 30 days for POC logs.

Stakeholders
- I will be the primary product contact; Priya (cc’d) owns platform/infra and will handle access and log exports. We’ll also loop in our security lead if needed for any data handling reviews.

Timeline
- 3-week POC is fine for us. Proposed kickoff: week of Jun 8 — we can take a 1-hour integration call that day.

Can you share the detailed observability checklist and a proposed kickoff calendar invite?

—Alex
Alex Turner
Product Manager, FinTechX
alex.turner@fintechx.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: FinTechX POC - Observability checklist & ownership (attached)

Alex / Priya —
Attached is the POC observability checklist I mentioned (redwood-poc-observability-checklist.xlsx). Summary below and explicit owners so nothing falls through the cracks.

POC observability deliverables (we’ll ship these during Week 0-2)
1) Dashboards (Redwood Console shared view + JSON dashboard defs) — owner: Jordan Blake
   - Route performance (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, cost per route
   - Error breakdown by status code and model variant
   - Embedding recall/precision chart for provided eval set (automated eval run)

2) Tracing
   - End-to-end traces including spans: incoming request, routing decision, model inference, KV cache lookup, response assembly
   - Tags: request_id, route, model_version, cache_hit (true/false) — owner: Sean Gallagher

3) Logs & Exports
   - Structured per-request logs (JSON) with redaction flags; S3 export to your bucket + Datadog forwarder configuration (30-day retention) — owner: Jordan + FinTechX platform (Priya)

4) Alerting & SLOs
   - Baseline alerts: p99 > 300ms, error rate > 0.5% over 5m window; SLOs documented in checklist

5) Evaluation harness
   - Automated run that scores embedding similarity on your eval set and compares baseline -> Redwood output; include A/B comparison and ROC/AUC tables — owner: Marissa (coord) + FinTechX data team

Timeline & milestones
- Week 0 (Jun 8): Kickoff + baseline run, access and log export validation
- Week 1 (Jun 9-15): Dashboards & tracing live, run first eval
- Week 2 (Jun 16-22): Optimization tweaks, re-run evals, cost tuning
- Week 3 (Jun 23): Final readout and decision meeting

Next steps (action items)
- I’ve uploaded the checklist and dashboard defs to the shared Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-fintechx-poc
- Jordan will prepare a shared console view and JSON export you can import.
- Priya / FinTechX: please confirm the S3 bucket path and we’ll validate exports during Week 0.
- I’ll create the kickoff calendar invite for week of Jun 8 — suggested: Tue Jun 9 10:00am PT.

Attachment: redwood-poc-observability-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
